# Co-DJ API — scripts, tools, hosts

An AI (or human) co-DJ is a **program**: a small JavaScript script whose hooks run against the live room every bar.
The same capabilities are exposed three ways, all generated from one registry
([src/agentkit/Commands.tish](../src/agentkit/Commands.tish)):

- **Script API** — `codj.<name>(…)` inside a co-DJ script (types: [public/codj.d.ts](../public/codj.d.ts), served at `/codj.d.ts`).
- **LLM tools** — the built-in Hypery co-DJ agent calls them (plus `write_script` / `read_script` / `run_script` / `script_logs`).
- **MCP tools** — `pnpm run mcp` exposes the same tools to Cursor / Claude ([services/mcp/main.tish](../services/mcp/main.tish)).

Agents are better at writing code than at driving long tool sequences, so the intended loop is: **read the room,
write the script, read its logs** — the script then plays on its own, bar after bar, and is rewritten when the
music (or the chat) calls for it.

## A script

```js
// examples/codj/hat-evolver.js
export function setup(codj) {
  if (!codj.owned().length) codj.state.hat = codj.addTrack({ name: 'Hat', gen: 'noise_burst', steps: '..x...x...x...x.' }).id
}
export function onBar(codj, ctx) {
  const fill = ctx.bar % 8 === 7
  codj.setSteps(codj.state.hat, fill ? 'x.xxx.xxx.xxx.xx' : '..x...x...x...x.')
}
```

| hook | when | writes land |
|---|---|---|
| `setup(codj, ctx)` | once per (re)load, after the room snapshot | now |
| `onBar(codj, ctx)` | every bar while playing (`ctx.bar`) | next bar |
| `onBeat(codj, ctx)` | every beat while playing (`ctx.beat`) | next beat |
| `onMessage(codj, ctx)` | someone chatted (`ctx.message`, `.toMe`) | next bar |
| `onEvent(codj, ctx)` | anything else the room published (`ctx.event`) | next bar |

`codj.state` survives hot reloads; `codj.log(…)` goes to the co-DJ's log. A script that fails to load (or whose
`setup` throws) never replaces the running one; one that throws three times in a row rolls back to the last good
source. Hooks have a 50 ms budget (enforced with `node:vm` in the CLI; the browser worker is watchdogged).

## Hosts

| host | how | identity |
|---|---|---|
| Browser | Co-DJ panel → **Add AI co-DJ** (producer) or **Add AI host** (session, booth, fader, echo/filter) — a Web Worker; loopback to this page, or the room when connected | your Hypery login |
| CLI | `pnpm run codj -- run examples/codj/hat-evolver.js --session <id> [--agent]` (file-watch hot reload) | `pnpm run codj:login` (browser login) |
| MCP | `pnpm run mcp` — tools for Cursor / Claude, same registry | `pnpm run codj:login` |

Everything a co-DJ sees comes from what the host publishes (deck deltas, snapshots, ticks, chat, edit results —
[STREAM_PROTOCOL.md §7](STREAM_PROTOCOL.md)); everything it does is deck text through the host's one gated ingest.

## Commands

| script | tool | kind | what |
|---|---|---|---|
| `codj.deck()` | `get_deck` | read | The whole session as deck text (the room's shared document, exactly as the host would save it). |
| `codj.tracks()` | `list_tracks` | read | Every track: id, name, gen, owner, mine, mix, a 16-char step string ('x' = hit), note count, bars, and onDeck (the deck letter it plays on). |
| `codj.track(id)` | `get_track` | read | One track in full: its summary + deck block text + generator params + piano notes. |
| `codj.owned()` | `list_owned` | read | Ids of the tracks this co-DJ owns (the only tracks it may edit). |
| `codj.clock()` | `get_clock` | read | The shared playhead: perfStep (16ths since play), bar, beat (0-3), step (0-15), bpm, playing. |
| `codj.room()` | `get_room` | read | Who is here: me ({actorId, displayName, skillIds, isHost}), host actorId, roster, what the host is focused on. |
| `codj.instruments()` | `list_instruments` | read | Every `gen` you can put on a track: the fixed generators and the macro voices, with descriptions. |
| `codj.grammar()` | `get_grammar` | read | The deck lines a co-DJ may write (track blocks, generator params, what is master-only). |
| `codj.preview(text)` | `preview_deck` | read | Dry-run deck text: which lines the host's gate would accept/reject (and why) and which tracks it would add/edit/remove. Nothing is sent. |
| `codj.send(text, opts?)` | `send_deck` | write | Send raw deck lines to the room (the general write — everything below is sugar over it). Lands at the next bar while playing. |
| `codj.library(kind?)` | `library` | read | The reference library: factory instruments, drum beats, melodic sequences, and full kits. Each row is {id, kind, role, name, about}. kind filters to 'instrument' \| 'beat' \| 'sequence' \| 'kit'. Pass an id to codj.preset, or put preset/beat/sequence on an arrange track. |
| `codj.preset(id)` | `preset` | read | One library entry. An instrument has gen + params (the knobs — pass them through, or codj.set(id, 'gen/<knob>', value)). A beat has steps and accent lanes. A sequence has events in semitones above defaultRoot. A kit has .parts, which is an arrange() argument: codj.arrange(codj.preset('house-loop').parts). |
| `codj.addTrack(spec, opts?)` | `add_track` | write | Add a track you own. spec: {name, gen, id?, preset?, beat?, sequence?, root?, steps?, notes?, gain?, pan?, params?, bars?}. preset/beat/sequence pull from the library (codj.library). Returns the new id. |
| `codj.arrange(tracks, opts?)` | `arrange` | write | Replace your whole arrangement in one call: removes EVERY track you own, then adds every track in the spec. A second arrange() deletes what the first one built — put the whole set in one call, and use addTrack to add one more part. With opts.deck ('A'..'D') it builds a song on that deck: only your tracks on that deck are replaced, the new tracks are placed there, and the ids are kept in codj.state.decks[deck] (codj.state.ids keeps pointing at the song on the other deck) — this is how you load the next song on a free deck (codj.session().free) while the current one plays. A track: {id?, name, gen, preset?, beat?, sequence?, root?, bars?, gain?, pan?, eq_lo?, eq_mid?, eq_hi?, params?, adsr?: {a,d,s,r}, fx?: {cutoff, res, drive, reverb_send, filter_type}, voice?: {octave, chord, arp, arprate, inversion, strum}, step_pitch?, steps?: 'x..x' \| 16 booleans \| 'euclid N', step_vel?, step_prob?, step_ratchet?, step_nudge? (16 numbers each), notes?: [{pitch, start, dur, vel, p?, r?, n?, bar?}]}. preset/beat/sequence expand from the library; fields you set win. Notes span the phrase: start runs 0..bars*4 beats. Returns {ids} mapping each spec id to its real track id (also stored on codj.state.ids). |
| `codj.setSteps(trackId, pattern, opts?)` | `set_steps` | write | Replace a track's 16-step pattern: 'x...x...x...x...' (spaces ok), 16 booleans, or 'euclid N'. A track plays either steps or notes, so this clears any piano notes. |
| `codj.setNotes(trackId, notes, opts?)` | `set_notes` | write | Replace a track's piano notes: [{pitch (MIDI), start (beats), dur (beats), vel (0-127)}]. [] clears. |
| `codj.mix(trackId, mix, opts?)` | `set_mix` | write | Set a track's mixer fields: {gain 0-1, pan -1..1, mute, solo, eq_lo/eq_mid/eq_hi dB}. Unset fields keep their value. |
| `codj.set(trackId, address, value, opts?)` | `set_param` | write | Set one addressed field on a track. Channel strip: 'fx/cutoff' (Hz) \| 'fx/res' (0..1) \| 'fx/drive' \| 'fx/reverb' \| 'fx/filter_type' (lowpass\|highpass\|bandpass\|notch) \| 'fx/lfo_rate' \| 'fx/lfo_depth'. Instrument: 'gen/<knob>' — knob names are the keys of codj.preset(id).params, different for every generator. Also 'voice/arp' \| 'voice/chord' \| 'voice/octave' \| 'adsr' ({a,d,s,r}) \| 'name' \| 'gen_type'. |
| `codj.knobs(trackId)` | `get_knobs` | read | Every knob on a live track, so you can play the instrument: {gen, knobs: [{knob, value, base (the instrument's default), min, max, unit, options?}], fx: {cutoff, res, drive, reverb, filter_type}, adsr}. Each knob is codj.set(trackId, 'gen/' + knob, value) (or codj.ride to sweep it). Knobs change the sound in real time while the pattern keeps playing — a filter opening, a decay getting longer, an FM index rising. |
| `codj.swap(trackId, instrument, params?, opts?)` | `swap_instrument` | write | Change the instrument a track plays, keeping its pattern, notes, mix and channel FX — the part carries on with a new sound (a pluck becomes a pad, an 808 becomes a reese). instrument: a gen from codj.instruments() ('pad', 'sub808', 'acid', …) or a library instrument id from codj.library('instrument') — a preset brings its knob settings. params overrides knobs after the swap. |
| `codj.ride(trackId, address, to, opts?)` | `ride_param` | write | Sweep one track field from where it is to `to` over the next bars, the way a hand rides a knob: a filter opening into a drop, a decay stretching across a breakdown, an FM index climbing, reverb swelling. address is any codj.set address ('gen/<knob>' from codj.knobs, 'fx/cutoff', 'fx/reverb', 'fx/drive', 'mix/gain', …). opts: {bars (default 4), from?, steps (moves per bar, default 2; at most 8 moves per ride), curve: 'linear' \| 'exp' (exp suits Hz)}. While stopped it jumps straight to `to`. One ride at a time per track — each move re-applies the track for everyone listening. |
| `codj.setGlobal(address, value, opts?)` | `set_global` | write | Master-scope edit (needs the master_mixer skill, i.e. a host): 'bpm' \| 'swing' \| 'scale' ({root 0-11, mode}) \| 'xfade' ({x, y} — prefer codj.crossfade) \| 'master/eq_lo' \| 'master/eq_mid' \| 'master/eq_hi' \| 'master/comp' \| 'master/reverb' \| 'actor/<lane>/gain' \| 'auto/<trackId>/<knob>' (16 step values). |
| `codj.removeTrack(trackId, opts?)` | `remove_track` | write | Remove one track. A host may remove any track, including the page-load starter (c0 Kick, c1 Snare, c2 HiHat, c3 Bass). A client may remove only a track it owns. |
| `codj.placeholder()` | `is_placeholder` | read | True while the page-load starter (ids c0 Kick, c1 Snare, c2 HiHat, c3 Bass) is still in the room and every other track is yours, even though the room stamps the starter as the local user. A host clears it before building its own sequence. A track someone else added or loaded makes this false. |
| `codj.clear(opts?)` | `clear_tracks` | write | Clean slate. A host removes every track (use this on the page-load starter, and whenever someone asks to start over). A client removes only the tracks it owns. opts.deck limits it to one deck — unload the outgoing song after a transition. Returns {removed: ids}. After clearing, arrange again — old codj.state.ids point at tracks that are gone. |
| `codj.launch(scene, deck?, opts?)` | `launch_scene` | write | Launch a session scene (host). 0-based; lands on the launch quantize. With deck ('A'..'D') only that deck's tracks move to the scene and the deck stays pinned there — the shared song and other decks are untouched (`@ launch scene N deck X`). Without deck, every unpinned track on every deck follows (`@ launch scene N`). When you run more than one deck, always pass the deck. |
| `codj.launchClip(trackId, clipId, opts?)` | `launch_clip` | write | Launch ONE track's clip over whatever scene is playing (`@ launch clip <trackId> <clipId>`) — the stem move: swap the hat to its 'busy' clip, the bass to its 'drop' clip, without changing the scene. It holds across scene changes until released. clipId '-' returns the track to its scene. Clip ids are in codj.session().rows[i].clips. |
| `codj.stopClip(trackId, opts?)` | `stop_clip` | write | Stop one track's clip (the ■ on its row): silent until a clip or scene is launched for it. Taking a stem out — the kick before a drop, the bass in a breakdown. |
| `codj.deckCtl(deck, action, opts?)` | `deck_control` | write | Host: 'stop' silences every track on a deck and keeps it silent (the outgoing song after a transition); 'song' releases the deck back to the shared session's scenes. |
| `codj.follow(scene, action, weighted?, opts?)` | `set_follow` | write | Host: a scene's follow action — the session's own dropdown (↻ Loop, → Next, ← Prev, ⏮ First, ⏭ Last, ✦ Any, ■ Stop). After the scene plays its length, the shared song does this. Add `other` with `chance` (0..100, the % for action) for the weighted second action (⚖): codj.follow(1, 'repeat', { other: 'next', chance: 75 }) loops 75% and moves on 25%. action null clears it (the scene loops). Drives scenes launched without a deck; a deck you pinned with launch(n, deck) is yours to move. |
| `codj.quantize(q, opts?)` | `launch_quantize` | write | Host: the launch quantize — where a launched scene or clip drops in. 'beat' \| 'bar' \| '2bar' \| '4bar' \| '8bar', or a step count (16 = one bar). Long quantize makes scene changes land on the phrase without counting bars yourself. |
| `codj.song(entries, opts?)` | `set_song` | write | Host: the shared song order — [{scene, repeat}] played top to bottom (0-based scenes, repeat = times through). [] clears it so a launched scene loops. Follow actions, when set, take precedence. |
| `codj.scenes(n, opts?)` | `session_scenes` | write | Host: set how many session scenes exist (`session_scenes N`). Default is 4. |
| `codj.clip(trackId, spec, opts?)` | `clip` | write | Host: save a pattern as one of a track's clips. spec: {clip?, scene? (0-based), name?, bars?, beat?, sequence?, root?, steps?, notes?}. The beat/sequence/steps become the clip; the track's instrument, EQ and FX stay on the channel and are mixed live. With scene it is slotted into that column; without, it goes into the track's bank for codj.launchClip — a stem variation (a busy hat, a halftime kick, a fill). |
| `codj.clips(track, list, opts?)` | `set_clips` | write | Host: give a track its numbered clips — the short patterns (1, 2 or 4 bars) a song is composed from in Session mode, like the clip slots a producer fills before arranging scenes. list[i] becomes clip #(i+1): a library beat or sequence id (codj.library('beat').filter(b => b.role === 'kick')), or a ClipSpec {beat?, sequence?, root?, steps?, notes?, bars?, name?}. Write 2–4 per track that differ in a way a listener hears (sparse / full / busy / a fill; root riff / answer phrase / held chords). Then codj.scene(n, { kick: 1, hat: 2, bass: 1 }) picks which number each track plays in each scene. Writes the bank only — nothing changes until a scene uses them. key is a track id or a spec id from arrange; opts.deck as in scene. |
| `codj.scene(scene, parts, name?, opts?)` | `set_scene` | write | Host: build one whole session column (scene n, 0-based) in one call. parts maps a track — its id, or its spec id from arrange (codj.state.ids) — to what it plays in this scene: a clip number from codj.clips (1, 2, 3 — the way to compose: pick a different number per scene), true (the track's own pattern), a library beat or sequence id ('four-on-the-floor', 'root-fifth'), a ClipSpec {beat?, sequence?, root?, steps?, notes?, bars?, clip?}, or null (silent). Every track you own ON THE SAME DECK that parts leaves out is silent in this scene, so each scene is a real arrangement: an intro with only kick and hat, a break with only the pad. name labels the clips (it becomes the clip id). opts.deck picks which song's ids to use when you run two decks. Grows the session if n is past the last scene. |
| `codj.cue(opts?)` | `cue_listen` | read | Listen in the headphones before you commit, like a DJ on the cue button. Reports how a session scene sounds — every part playing (role, band, hits a bar, clip), the low / mid / high bands, warnings (too many parts, mud in the low end, two leads fighting, too busy) and a verdict: silent \| sparse \| balanced \| busy \| cluttered. opts: {scene? (default: the scene you last launched on deck), deck?, change?}. change previews a change WITHOUT sending it, with the same values as codj.scene parts: { hook: null } takes a part out, { hat: 3 } swaps its clip, { keys: { gen: 'pad', sequence: 'axis-min7' } } adds a new part. The result also has before (the scene as it is) so you can compare. If the verdict after a change is busy or cluttered, do not add — take something away or move it to another scene. |
| `codj.session()` | `get_session` | read | The session grid: scenes (column count), deck (the deck your first track is on, or null), rows [{trackId, name, mine, deck, slots: clipId per scene ('' when silent or only its default pattern), clips: the track's clip bank — every clip you can launchClip}], filled (how many of YOUR tracks play in each scene), decks ({B: {tracks, filled}} for each deck you have tracks on), and free (decks you may load a song onto: yours, and decks no other player holds). |
| `codj.play(mode?, opts?)` | `transport_play` | write | Host: start the shared transport. 'song' plays the launched session; 'sequence' (or 'seq') plays the rack you are editing. |
| `codj.stop(opts?)` | `transport_stop` | write | Host: stop the shared transport. |
| `codj.crossfade(x, y, opts?)` | `crossfade` | write | Host: move the 4-way fader. x is left-right (0 = deck A, 1 = deck B, 0.5 = both). y is top-bottom (0 = decks A/B, 1 = decks C/D, 0.5 = both). Equal-power, so the center is full and a corner is one deck. |
| `codj.booth(deck, spec, opts?)` | `booth` | write | Host: one deck's booth strip. deck is 'A'\|'B'\|'C'\|'D'. spec: {hi, mid, lo} in dB (-12..12), flt (-1..0 closes a lowpass; 0 is open), vol (0..1). This is the mixer EQ and filter for every track on that deck, separate from a track's own fx/cutoff. |
| `codj.throwFx(type, on, params?, opts?)` | `throw_fx` | write | Host: punch a master effect on the whole mix, then release it. type 'echo' (params {time in seconds <=2, fb 0..0.9}) or 'filter' (params {freq in Hz}; on closes the master lowpass, off opens it back to full). This is a performance throw, not a track send. On for a bar or two of a build, off into the drop. |
| `codj.blend(to, opts?)` | `blend_decks` | write | Host: schedule a whole transition ahead of time, the way a DJ cues the next record and knows the bar it comes in on. Once called, every step lands on time by itself — nothing else has to run. opts: {bar (absolute bar the mix starts on; default the next 8-bar phrase at least 8 bars away), bars (4..64, default 16), style: 'blend' (incoming intro with its bass cut, the fader glides corner to corner, the bass swaps halfway, the outgoing deck stops at the end) \| 'cut' (switch on the one) \| 'echo' (the outgoing song echoes out over the cut), scene (incoming scene to start on, default 0), swapScene (incoming scene at the bass swap, default 1; -1 keeps the first), from (default: the deck the fader sits on)}. Build and cue the incoming song on its deck first; it stays silent until the bar. Returns the plan and records it on codj.state.blend. |
| `codj.say(text, to?)` | `say` | write | Chat to the room; `to` (actorId or display name) addresses one co-DJ. |

## Tools (LLM / MCP names)

- `get_deck` (read) — The whole session as deck text (the room's shared document, exactly as the host would save it).
- `list_tracks` (read) — Every track: id, name, gen, owner, mine, mix, a 16-char step string ('x' = hit), note count, bars, and onDeck (the deck letter it plays on).
- `get_track` (read) — One track in full: its summary + deck block text + generator params + piano notes.
- `list_owned` (read) — Ids of the tracks this co-DJ owns (the only tracks it may edit).
- `get_clock` (read) — The shared playhead: perfStep (16ths since play), bar, beat (0-3), step (0-15), bpm, playing.
- `get_room` (read) — Who is here: me ({actorId, displayName, skillIds, isHost}), host actorId, roster, what the host is focused on.
- `list_instruments` (read) — Every `gen` you can put on a track: the fixed generators and the macro voices, with descriptions.
- `get_grammar` (read) — The deck lines a co-DJ may write (track blocks, generator params, what is master-only).
- `preview_deck` (read) — Dry-run deck text: which lines the host's gate would accept/reject (and why) and which tracks it would add/edit/remove. Nothing is sent.
- `send_deck` — Send raw deck lines to the room (the general write — everything below is sugar over it). Lands at the next bar while playing.
- `library` (read) — The reference library: factory instruments, drum beats, melodic sequences, and full kits. Each row is {id, kind, role, name, about}. kind filters to 'instrument' | 'beat' | 'sequence' | 'kit'. Pass an id to codj.preset, or put preset/beat/sequence on an arrange track.
- `preset` (read) — One library entry. An instrument has gen + params (the knobs — pass them through, or codj.set(id, 'gen/<knob>', value)). A beat has steps and accent lanes. A sequence has events in semitones above defaultRoot. A kit has .parts, which is an arrange() argument: codj.arrange(codj.preset('house-loop').parts).
- `add_track` — Add a track you own. spec: {name, gen, id?, preset?, beat?, sequence?, root?, steps?, notes?, gain?, pan?, params?, bars?}. preset/beat/sequence pull from the library (codj.library). Returns the new id.
- `arrange` — Replace your whole arrangement in one call: removes EVERY track you own, then adds every track in the spec. A second arrange() deletes what the first one built — put the whole set in one call, and use addTrack to add one more part. With opts.deck ('A'..'D') it builds a song on that deck: only your tracks on that deck are replaced, the new tracks are placed there, and the ids are kept in codj.state.decks[deck] (codj.state.ids keeps pointing at the song on the other deck) — this is how you load the next song on a free deck (codj.session().free) while the current one plays. A track: {id?, name, gen, preset?, beat?, sequence?, root?, bars?, gain?, pan?, eq_lo?, eq_mid?, eq_hi?, params?, adsr?: {a,d,s,r}, fx?: {cutoff, res, drive, reverb_send, filter_type}, voice?: {octave, chord, arp, arprate, inversion, strum}, step_pitch?, steps?: 'x..x' | 16 booleans | 'euclid N', step_vel?, step_prob?, step_ratchet?, step_nudge? (16 numbers each), notes?: [{pitch, start, dur, vel, p?, r?, n?, bar?}]}. preset/beat/sequence expand from the library; fields you set win. Notes span the phrase: start runs 0..bars*4 beats. Returns {ids} mapping each spec id to its real track id (also stored on codj.state.ids).
- `set_steps` — Replace a track's 16-step pattern: 'x...x...x...x...' (spaces ok), 16 booleans, or 'euclid N'. A track plays either steps or notes, so this clears any piano notes.
- `set_notes` — Replace a track's piano notes: [{pitch (MIDI), start (beats), dur (beats), vel (0-127)}]. [] clears.
- `set_mix` — Set a track's mixer fields: {gain 0-1, pan -1..1, mute, solo, eq_lo/eq_mid/eq_hi dB}. Unset fields keep their value.
- `set_param` — Set one addressed field on a track. Channel strip: 'fx/cutoff' (Hz) | 'fx/res' (0..1) | 'fx/drive' | 'fx/reverb' | 'fx/filter_type' (lowpass|highpass|bandpass|notch) | 'fx/lfo_rate' | 'fx/lfo_depth'. Instrument: 'gen/<knob>' — knob names are the keys of codj.preset(id).params, different for every generator. Also 'voice/arp' | 'voice/chord' | 'voice/octave' | 'adsr' ({a,d,s,r}) | 'name' | 'gen_type'.
- `get_knobs` (read) — Every knob on a live track, so you can play the instrument: {gen, knobs: [{knob, value, base (the instrument's default), min, max, unit, options?}], fx: {cutoff, res, drive, reverb, filter_type}, adsr}. Each knob is codj.set(trackId, 'gen/' + knob, value) (or codj.ride to sweep it). Knobs change the sound in real time while the pattern keeps playing — a filter opening, a decay getting longer, an FM index rising.
- `swap_instrument` — Change the instrument a track plays, keeping its pattern, notes, mix and channel FX — the part carries on with a new sound (a pluck becomes a pad, an 808 becomes a reese). instrument: a gen from codj.instruments() ('pad', 'sub808', 'acid', …) or a library instrument id from codj.library('instrument') — a preset brings its knob settings. params overrides knobs after the swap.
- `ride_param` — Sweep one track field from where it is to `to` over the next bars, the way a hand rides a knob: a filter opening into a drop, a decay stretching across a breakdown, an FM index climbing, reverb swelling. address is any codj.set address ('gen/<knob>' from codj.knobs, 'fx/cutoff', 'fx/reverb', 'fx/drive', 'mix/gain', …). opts: {bars (default 4), from?, steps (moves per bar, default 2; at most 8 moves per ride), curve: 'linear' | 'exp' (exp suits Hz)}. While stopped it jumps straight to `to`. One ride at a time per track — each move re-applies the track for everyone listening.
- `set_global` — Master-scope edit (needs the master_mixer skill, i.e. a host): 'bpm' | 'swing' | 'scale' ({root 0-11, mode}) | 'xfade' ({x, y} — prefer codj.crossfade) | 'master/eq_lo' | 'master/eq_mid' | 'master/eq_hi' | 'master/comp' | 'master/reverb' | 'actor/<lane>/gain' | 'auto/<trackId>/<knob>' (16 step values).
- `remove_track` — Remove one track. A host may remove any track, including the page-load starter (c0 Kick, c1 Snare, c2 HiHat, c3 Bass). A client may remove only a track it owns.
- `is_placeholder` (read) — True while the page-load starter (ids c0 Kick, c1 Snare, c2 HiHat, c3 Bass) is still in the room and every other track is yours, even though the room stamps the starter as the local user. A host clears it before building its own sequence. A track someone else added or loaded makes this false.
- `clear_tracks` — Clean slate. A host removes every track (use this on the page-load starter, and whenever someone asks to start over). A client removes only the tracks it owns. opts.deck limits it to one deck — unload the outgoing song after a transition. Returns {removed: ids}. After clearing, arrange again — old codj.state.ids point at tracks that are gone.
- `launch_scene` — Launch a session scene (host). 0-based; lands on the launch quantize. With deck ('A'..'D') only that deck's tracks move to the scene and the deck stays pinned there — the shared song and other decks are untouched (`@ launch scene N deck X`). Without deck, every unpinned track on every deck follows (`@ launch scene N`). When you run more than one deck, always pass the deck.
- `launch_clip` — Launch ONE track's clip over whatever scene is playing (`@ launch clip <trackId> <clipId>`) — the stem move: swap the hat to its 'busy' clip, the bass to its 'drop' clip, without changing the scene. It holds across scene changes until released. clipId '-' returns the track to its scene. Clip ids are in codj.session().rows[i].clips.
- `stop_clip` — Stop one track's clip (the ■ on its row): silent until a clip or scene is launched for it. Taking a stem out — the kick before a drop, the bass in a breakdown.
- `deck_control` — Host: 'stop' silences every track on a deck and keeps it silent (the outgoing song after a transition); 'song' releases the deck back to the shared session's scenes.
- `set_follow` — Host: a scene's follow action — the session's own dropdown (↻ Loop, → Next, ← Prev, ⏮ First, ⏭ Last, ✦ Any, ■ Stop). After the scene plays its length, the shared song does this. Add `other` with `chance` (0..100, the % for action) for the weighted second action (⚖): codj.follow(1, 'repeat', { other: 'next', chance: 75 }) loops 75% and moves on 25%. action null clears it (the scene loops). Drives scenes launched without a deck; a deck you pinned with launch(n, deck) is yours to move.
- `launch_quantize` — Host: the launch quantize — where a launched scene or clip drops in. 'beat' | 'bar' | '2bar' | '4bar' | '8bar', or a step count (16 = one bar). Long quantize makes scene changes land on the phrase without counting bars yourself.
- `set_song` — Host: the shared song order — [{scene, repeat}] played top to bottom (0-based scenes, repeat = times through). [] clears it so a launched scene loops. Follow actions, when set, take precedence.
- `session_scenes` — Host: set how many session scenes exist (`session_scenes N`). Default is 4.
- `clip` — Host: save a pattern as one of a track's clips. spec: {clip?, scene? (0-based), name?, bars?, beat?, sequence?, root?, steps?, notes?}. The beat/sequence/steps become the clip; the track's instrument, EQ and FX stay on the channel and are mixed live. With scene it is slotted into that column; without, it goes into the track's bank for codj.launchClip — a stem variation (a busy hat, a halftime kick, a fill).
- `set_clips` — Host: give a track its numbered clips — the short patterns (1, 2 or 4 bars) a song is composed from in Session mode, like the clip slots a producer fills before arranging scenes. list[i] becomes clip #(i+1): a library beat or sequence id (codj.library('beat').filter(b => b.role === 'kick')), or a ClipSpec {beat?, sequence?, root?, steps?, notes?, bars?, name?}. Write 2–4 per track that differ in a way a listener hears (sparse / full / busy / a fill; root riff / answer phrase / held chords). Then codj.scene(n, { kick: 1, hat: 2, bass: 1 }) picks which number each track plays in each scene. Writes the bank only — nothing changes until a scene uses them. key is a track id or a spec id from arrange; opts.deck as in scene.
- `set_scene` — Host: build one whole session column (scene n, 0-based) in one call. parts maps a track — its id, or its spec id from arrange (codj.state.ids) — to what it plays in this scene: a clip number from codj.clips (1, 2, 3 — the way to compose: pick a different number per scene), true (the track's own pattern), a library beat or sequence id ('four-on-the-floor', 'root-fifth'), a ClipSpec {beat?, sequence?, root?, steps?, notes?, bars?, clip?}, or null (silent). Every track you own ON THE SAME DECK that parts leaves out is silent in this scene, so each scene is a real arrangement: an intro with only kick and hat, a break with only the pad. name labels the clips (it becomes the clip id). opts.deck picks which song's ids to use when you run two decks. Grows the session if n is past the last scene.
- `cue_listen` (read) — Listen in the headphones before you commit, like a DJ on the cue button. Reports how a session scene sounds — every part playing (role, band, hits a bar, clip), the low / mid / high bands, warnings (too many parts, mud in the low end, two leads fighting, too busy) and a verdict: silent | sparse | balanced | busy | cluttered. opts: {scene? (default: the scene you last launched on deck), deck?, change?}. change previews a change WITHOUT sending it, with the same values as codj.scene parts: { hook: null } takes a part out, { hat: 3 } swaps its clip, { keys: { gen: 'pad', sequence: 'axis-min7' } } adds a new part. The result also has before (the scene as it is) so you can compare. If the verdict after a change is busy or cluttered, do not add — take something away or move it to another scene.
- `get_session` (read) — The session grid: scenes (column count), deck (the deck your first track is on, or null), rows [{trackId, name, mine, deck, slots: clipId per scene ('' when silent or only its default pattern), clips: the track's clip bank — every clip you can launchClip}], filled (how many of YOUR tracks play in each scene), decks ({B: {tracks, filled}} for each deck you have tracks on), and free (decks you may load a song onto: yours, and decks no other player holds).
- `transport_play` — Host: start the shared transport. 'song' plays the launched session; 'sequence' (or 'seq') plays the rack you are editing.
- `transport_stop` — Host: stop the shared transport.
- `crossfade` — Host: move the 4-way fader. x is left-right (0 = deck A, 1 = deck B, 0.5 = both). y is top-bottom (0 = decks A/B, 1 = decks C/D, 0.5 = both). Equal-power, so the center is full and a corner is one deck.
- `booth` — Host: one deck's booth strip. deck is 'A'|'B'|'C'|'D'. spec: {hi, mid, lo} in dB (-12..12), flt (-1..0 closes a lowpass; 0 is open), vol (0..1). This is the mixer EQ and filter for every track on that deck, separate from a track's own fx/cutoff.
- `throw_fx` — Host: punch a master effect on the whole mix, then release it. type 'echo' (params {time in seconds <=2, fb 0..0.9}) or 'filter' (params {freq in Hz}; on closes the master lowpass, off opens it back to full). This is a performance throw, not a track send. On for a bar or two of a build, off into the drop.
- `blend_decks` — Host: schedule a whole transition ahead of time, the way a DJ cues the next record and knows the bar it comes in on. Once called, every step lands on time by itself — nothing else has to run. opts: {bar (absolute bar the mix starts on; default the next 8-bar phrase at least 8 bars away), bars (4..64, default 16), style: 'blend' (incoming intro with its bass cut, the fader glides corner to corner, the bass swaps halfway, the outgoing deck stops at the end) | 'cut' (switch on the one) | 'echo' (the outgoing song echoes out over the cut), scene (incoming scene to start on, default 0), swapScene (incoming scene at the bass swap, default 1; -1 keeps the first), from (default: the deck the fader sits on)}. Build and cue the incoming song on its deck first; it stays silent until the bar. Returns the plan and records it on codj.state.blend.
- `say` — Chat to the room; `to` (actorId or display name) addresses one co-DJ.
